rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §1 puts the description copy, the compiled-signal application, the homogeneous_time rule and the on-disk write layout behind one module `imas_ambix/data/pulse_mint.py` and one function `mint_pulse` returning a receipt, so the interface is smaller than the behaviour it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements IDS assembly-and-write in `pulse_mint.py` without naming the existing owner to extend, `nova/io/egress.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 accounts for the one public function and one command it adds and states why nothing is retired (no data CLI command writes an IDS — verified: the 13 `@data.command` entries in `imas_ambix/data/cli.py` all read, fetch or write token stores), but §4 adds a figure-script option without naming what it retires or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §1 and §2 cite ambix's machinery and nova only as an equilibrium-topology finder, but the plan never searches nova's IDS assembly/egress owner (`nova/io/egress.py` `IdsEgress`, `nova/imas/ids_entry.py` `IdsEntry`) nor ambix's other IDS writers.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §1's `mint` command is a thin entry over the one function (justified), and §4 extends `scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py` rather than adding a parallel script and states the reason (a rendering change stays an imas-ink change).
